title: recording whose media file was modified seconds ago (or is dated in the future) is reported ELIGIBLE: the command never reads the media file mtime, so a stale processedAt on a re-recorded or in-progress file passes
evidence: Temp fixture, tenant toc, real clock. Session justwritten: source.json {_id:justwritten-src,tenantId:toc,kind:recording,path:justwritten.webm}; session.json status transcribe=done,index=done, processedAt=now-30d; one verified claim citing its turn; media/justwritten.webm 10 bytes with mtime=now-5000ms. Command with --min-age-days 7 --clip-padding-seconds 15 prints: RECORDING justwritten-src => ELIGIBLE (age: 30.0 d since processedAt). Same with media mtime=now+9 days (future-mtime-src => ELIGIBLE). Brief requirement: in-progress, re-recorded or clock-skewed recording must be KEEP.
fix_direction: Downgrade-only guard in the command: when the media file is present and its mtime is later than processedAt, or within the min-age window of now, or in the future, force KEEP with a named reason (media modified after processedAt / media mtime in the future). When mtime cannot be read (no --media-root) do not mark ELIGIBLE. Regression: the two fixtures above.
tier: security (destructive-adjacent; owner will pick thresholds from this report)

title: recording whose media file is missing, not located, or outside --media-root is still printed ELIGIBLE (size unknown); file state is informational and cannot change a verdict
area: packages/ingest/src/retention-report.ts preconditions() and section(); retention-report-state.ts mediaFile()
evidence: Fixture e-nomedia (all state valid, media file absent): RECORDING e-nomedia-src => ELIGIBLE with file=FAIL(missing), counted in 'eligible: 2 recording(s)'. Fixtures with source.json path ..\..\outside.webm and C:\Windows\win.ini: both ELIGIBLE, file '(not located)'. Without --media-root every recording has file=unknown yet is ELIGIBLE. The eligible COUNT includes recordings whose file the report could not confirm; only bytes are flagged unknown.
fix_direction: Report KEEP with reason 'media file not confirmed (missing | not located | no --media-root)', or print a separate eligible-unconfirmed bucket in TOTALS.

title: two state rows pointing at the SAME media file are judged independently: the file is printed ELIGIBLE on the strength of one row while another row for the same file is KEEP, and the bytes are counted once per row
area: packages/ingest/src/retention-report.ts section() (per-row verdict, no media-identity grouping)
evidence: Temp fixture, tenant toc, now injected, --min-age-days 7. Sessions dupA and dupB, both source.json path m/shared.webm (one 100-byte file, mtime now-30d, processedAt now-30d), dupB has one needs-review claim citing its turn. Output: RECORDING dupA-src => ELIGIBLE; RECORDING dupB-src => KEEP (1 claim(s) citing this media are not yet verified); TOTALS eligible: 1 recording(s), 100 B | kept: 1 recording(s), 100 B (same file in both buckets). Second fixture: sessions A,B,C with paths m/shared.webm, m/./shared.webm, M/SHARED.WEBM (same file on Windows, all valid): all three ELIGIBLE, TOTALS eligible: 3 recording(s), 300 B for one 100-byte file. Planner dedupes only by source _id, not by file.
fix_direction: Downgrade-only grouping in the command: key rows by the realpath (case-folded on win32) of the stat'd file; if more than one row references a file, it is ELIGIBLE only when EVERY referencing row is planner-eligible with no guard hit, otherwise every row for it is KEEP with a named guard (media-shared-with-kept-row); count a shared file's bytes once; print a 'files referenced by more than one recording' line. Regression: the two fixtures above, measured by issue id.
tier: security (destructive-adjacent; the owner will choose purge thresholds from this report)

title: the report prints no as-of instant and does not sanity-check `now`: a system clock set years ahead makes every recording look old and ELIGIBLE with no warning
evidence: Fixture: session processedAt now-(1d+30m), media mtime now-1d, size recorded absent, --min-age-days 7 is not met at real time, but run with the injected now = real now + 5 years: RECORDING q-src => ELIGIBLE, no warning, and the output contains no timestamp at all (regex for an ISO instant in the output: false). A clock years BEHIND is handled (processedAt 'in the future' KEEP, media mtime clock-skew); a clock AHEAD is not detectable from a single recording but is from the corpus (e.g. newest media mtime or processedAt far older than the others).
fix_direction: Print 'as of <ISO now>' in the header so the owner can see the clock used; warn (and optionally refuse verdicts) when now is more than a stated bound after the newest mtime/processedAt in the data root while recent recordings exist, or earlier than the newest one.

title: in-progress and unreadable-file signals beyond mtime are unused: an ACL-denied file is ELIGIBLE (stat succeeds through the directory-listing fallback) and no read-only open probe or pipeline state is consulted
area: packages/ingest/src/retention-report-media.ts probeMedia(); scripts/webinar/run-pipeline.mjs operations.json (status recording/processing + artifact path)
evidence: Temp fixture: icacls /inheritance:r and /deny <user>:(F) on m/acl.webm (100 bytes, mtime now-30d, everything else valid): RECORDING acl-src => ELIGIBLE (size 100 B); the same deny on the parent directory gives media-unreadable (KEEP, not assessable). So a file the tool's own account cannot open is reported purgeable. A file held open by a writer is not detectable either (mtime is updated lazily for open handles on Windows). The webinar pipeline keeps per-webinar status recording|processing|failed with the artifact path in operations.json (run-pipeline.mjs:65, :203-212); the command never reads it.
fix_direction: Downgrade-only: after stat, attempt a read-only open (openSync(path,'r'), permitted by the scanner) and close; EACCES/EBUSY/EPERM -> media-unreadable (not assessable). Optionally read the pipeline operations store read-only and KEEP any recording whose artifact path matches a row with status recording|processing. Regression: the ACL fixture above.

title: a session record that cannot be read or parsed (truncated source.json after a crash, or a session directory whose name fails the name pattern) does NOT veto: a file it may reference is printed ELIGIBLE on the strength of the readable record that shares it
area: packages/ingest/src/retention-report-state.ts gatherState() (unreadable -> info.unreadable, no keys; names filter silently drops odd directory names) and retention-report/assess.ts (only located records form groups)
evidence: Temp fixture, tenant toc, --min-age-days 7, empty operations file, now NOW. Sessions good (path m/s.webm, 100 bytes, mtime now-30d, processedAt now-30d, verified claim) and trunc (source.json truncated: {"_id":"trunc-src","tenantId":"toc","kind":"rec ; session.json valid; its real source path was m/s.webm). Output: RECORDING good-src => ELIGIBLE; RECORDING trunc => KEEP (unreadable state); header says 'unreadable session records: 1 (their media paths are unknown and could reference any file)'; TOTALS eligible 1 recording, 100 B. Second fixture: the sibling session directory is named 'bad name' (space; fails SESSION_NAME): good-src => ELIGIBLE and the header says 'recordings: 1 ... unreadable session records: 0' - the directory is not counted or warned about at all.
fix_direction: Fail closed: if ANY session record in scope is unreadable (unparseable source.json/session.json, wrong kind type, or a directory skipped by the name filter) then no recording is ELIGIBLE (each eligible one becomes KEEP 'unreadable-records-present', not assessable) and the header names how many records and which directories; the unreadable record's referenced file is unknown so no file can be proven unreferenced. Count and warn about name-filtered directories too. Regression: both fixtures above, verbatim.
tier: security (destructive-adjacent; wrong ELIGIBLE with plausible crash state)

title: the command reads only the named tenant's directory, so a media file also referenced by another tenant's session record is printed ELIGIBLE; 'other-tenant records count as members' covers only records planted INSIDE this tenant's directory
evidence: Temp fixture, data root with tenant dirs toc and other (sha-256 segments). toc/mine: path m/s.webm, all valid, eligible. other/theirs: path m/s.webm, one needs-review claim. Run --tenant toc: RECORDING mine-src => ELIGIBLE, TOTALS eligible 1 recording, 100 B; nothing in the report mentions that another tenant's directory exists or may share files. A record with source.json tenantId 'other' placed inside toc's own directory is correctly a veto (shared-media-not-all-eligible).
fix_direction: Either (a) key-only pass over sibling tenant directories (read source.json path only, compute identity keys, print nothing about the other tenant beyond 'shared with a record outside this tenant'), or (b) at minimum print in the header and in the 'ELIGIBLE means' text that other tenants' directories are not read and ELIGIBLE says nothing about files they may reference, and make the executor unit's own re-check mandatory. Regression: the fixture above.

title: when the pipeline operations state is omitted or unreadable, media untouched for more than 30 days is still reported ELIGIBLE, so a recording stuck in processing/failed for over a month (a long backlog) is offered for purge
area: packages/ingest/src/retention-report/ops.ts opsGuard() unavailable branch (OPS_UNKNOWN_WINDOW_MS); --operations-state optional in retention-report-args.ts
evidence: Temp fixture: session stuck, processedAt now-60d, media mtime now-70d, 10 bytes, valid claims; command run WITHOUT --operations-state (header carries the PIPELINE STATE UNAVAILABLE warning): RECORDING stuck-src => ELIGIBLE. With an operations file containing {"operations":{"stuck":{"status":"processing"}}} the same recording is KEEP operation-in-progress.
fix_direction: Make --operations-state required like --media-root and thresholds, or make unavailable state behave as a refusal: no recording ELIGIBLE at all (operation-state-unavailable for every otherwise-eligible row regardless of age), with the existing header warning. An explicit opt-out flag (e.g. --no-operations-state-i-accept-risk) is acceptable only if its value is printed in the report header. Regression: the fixture above with the option omitted, with a missing file and with malformed JSON.
